title: Constructibility of the reduced geometric fibre locus
statement: Let $f:X\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], quasi-compact and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Assume $T$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For each $t\in T$ let $X_{\bar t}$ be the geometric fibre obtained by base change to a chosen algebraic closure of $\kappa(t)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Then the subset $E_f=\{t\in T\mid X_{\bar t}\text{ is reduced}\}$ is constructible in $T$ [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Reduced means that every local ring has no nonzero nilpotents [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Empty geometric fibres count as reduced. Neither flatness of $f$ nor a Noetherian hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0579 (lemma-geometrically-reduced-constructible), with topology.tex Tag 053W (lemma-collate-constructible) on a finite affine cover of the qcqs base. The geometric-fibre convention is equivalent to geometric reducedness by varieties.tex Tag 035X (lemma-geometrically-reduced), (2) iff (6), in positive characteristic and Tag 020I (lemma-perfect-reduced) in characteristic zero.

proof.text: Fix $t\in T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis] choose an affine open neighbourhood $V$ of $t$. Since $f$ is quasi-compact, $f^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact and has a finite affine open cover $U_1,\ldots,U_n$ by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover]. Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $U_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation] to the original locally finitely presented morphism $f$, the affine open $U_i\subseteq X$, and the affine open $V\subseteq T$, with $f(U_i)\subseteq V$. It gives that the induced ring map $A\to B_i$ is finitely presented. The affine theorem [lem-trf-geometrically-reduced-fibre-locus] gives constructibility of the locus where $\operatorname{Spec}(B_i\otimes_A\kappa(v))$ is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(v)$. Apply [lem-trf-geometric-reducedness-algebraic-closure-test] to this fibre, with $k=\kappa(v)$ and the algebraic closure chosen in the item. Its all-field-extension condition is exactly the affine theorem's condition; its other condition is reducedness of $(U_i)_{\bar v}$. Thus the constructible locus is precisely $E_i=\{v\in V\mid (U_i)_{\bar v}\text{ is reduced}\}$. This comparison works in every characteristic, including empty chart fibres.

source.place: Tag 0579, affine-base and finite affine source-cover reduction; varieties.tex Tags 035X (2) iff (6) and 020I for the comparison with the chosen-algebraic-closure convention. Morphisms Tag 01TQ (lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize), (1) implies (2), supplies finite presentation of the chart ring map.

proof.text: For every $v\in V$, the fibre $(f^{-1}(V))_v$ is covered by the open subschemes $(U_i)_v$. A scheme is reduced exactly when all members of an open cover are reduced, so its geometric fibre is reduced exactly when every $(U_i)_{\bar v}$ is reduced. Consequently $E\cap V=\bigcap_{i=1}^n E_i$. Finite intersections preserve constructibility by the Boolean-algebra definition of [def-weil-constructible-subset].

source.place: Tag 0579, proof: fibres of the finite affine cover form an affine open covering of the fibre

proof.text: Thus every point $t\in T$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ for which $E\cap V$ is constructible. This is precisely that $E$ is locally constructible in the topological sense used by [lem-trf-locally-constructible-qcqs-global].

source.place: Tag 0579, first sentence of the proof (definition of locally constructible)

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-locally-constructible-qcqs-global] to the qcqs scheme $T$ and the subset $E$. It yields that $E$ is constructible in $T$. The empty-source and empty-fibre cases are included: the corresponding loci are all of $V$ and the reducedness criterion for an empty scheme is vacuous.
